areas.purpose: Reduce crushed bauxite (-25 mm) to a pumpable caustic slurry (100 % < 1 mm, P80 ~250-400 um) in hot spent ('mill') liquor at a controlled bauxite-to-liquor charge, and buffer it ahead of pre-desilication. Grinding exposes the gibbsite and kaolinite surfaces so that desilication and the short low-temperature digestion go to completion. It also keeps the residue coarse enough to settle and wash. A04 is the single owner of the mill feed bins and weigh feeders; they are not duplicated in the stockyard area A03.
areas.process_description:
1) Blended crushed bauxite (-25 mm top size, ~10 % free moisture, F80 ~10-20 mm - engineering estimate) is reclaimed from the bauxite stockyard (A03) by belt conveyor. A shuttle/tripper distributes it to four mill feed bins: 3 grinding lines operating + 1 standby, each line rated for ~1/3 of plant feed plus ~10-15 % margin. Design dry feed is 640 t/h at a bauxite factor of 2.65 t/t, which is the plant-wide value.
2) A weigh-belt feeder under each bin meters ~213 t/h dry (~237 t/h wet) bauxite into the mill feed chute. Hot mill liquor is added in the feed chute: strong spent liquor, C ~270-290 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C ~0.36-0.38, heated to ~88-95 degC in the mill liquor heater using digestion blow-off vapour (A07). A ratio controller sets the liquor flow to the dry bauxite rate, with bauxite moisture compensation, to give ~50-55 % solids w/w in the mill. The total bauxite-to-caustic 'charge' across grinding and digestion liquor is the main lever on digester A/C. The dry feed rate is therefore measured very carefully: weightometer plus moisture analyser/lab moisture.
3) Wet overflow ball mills (nominal 4.4 m dia x 6.5 m EGL, ~2 MW) grind the ore with a graded ball charge (make-up ~75-90 mm). Hot caustic begins to react. A small part of the gibbsite dissolves: Al(OH)3 + NaOH -> NaAl(OH)4. Kaolinite (reactive silica) also starts to dissolve: Al2Si2O5(OH)4 + 6 NaOH -> 2 NaAl(OH)4 + 2 Na2SiO3 + H2O. Mill power and reaction raise the temperature by a few degC.
4) Mill discharge passes through a trommel bolted to the discharge trunnion. Scats go to a scats bunker: hard caprock/laterite lumps >~8-12 mm, tramp metal and worn balls. Slurry falls into the mill discharge pump box, where extra liquor brings it to ~45-48 % solids for screening.
5) Mill discharge pumps lift the slurry to a flow divider. There is one duty and one installed standby per mill, all hard-metal centrifugal slurry pumps. The divider feeds multi-deck high-frequency screens with 1.0 mm polyurethane panels on an elevated screen floor.
6) Screen oversize returns by gravity chute to the mill feed chute (closed circuit). Circulating load is ~80-150 % (engineering estimate). Screen undersize (product) flows by gravity launder to two agitated slurry storage tanks. Together they give ~4-5 h surge at design rate and decouple grinding from pre-desilication and digestion.
7) Slurry transfer pumps deliver ~830 m3/h of slurry to the pre-desilication heaters (A05) at a rate set by digestion feed demand. Slurry conditions: SG ~1.65-1.72, 44-48 % solids, ~85-93 degC.
Control philosophy:
- Charge control: bauxite dry tph and the liquor:bauxite ratio, fed forward from the digestion A/C target.
- Mill load: mill power, sound and bearing pressure.
- Pump-box level: VFD on the mill discharge pump.
- Product size: online PSD analyser plus shift sieve.
- Storage tank levels.
- Slurry density: radiometric or Coriolis.
High-temperature (boehmitic) plants: the grinding circuit is essentially the same. Lime is often added at the mill for titanate scale and phosphate control, and the grind may be finer.

equipment.name: Mill feed bins and weigh-belt feeders
equipment.function: Provide ~2-4 h live surge of crushed bauxite in front of each mill and meter a precisely known dry bauxite rate into the mill (charge control). A04 is the single owner; A03 ends at the bin-top tripper.
equipment.qty_standby: 1 bin + 1 feeder (standby mill line)
equipment.type_selected: Steel bin with a mass-flow-profile slotted transition hopper, discharging onto a variable-speed weigh-belt feeder (load-cell idler + speed sensor).
equipment.why_this_type: Wet clayey bauxite (8-12 % moisture, fines) is cohesive and prone to rat-holing. A steep slotted hopper with a belt feeder gives more reliable flow than a vibrating feeder. The weigh-belt provides the tph signal for caustic-to-bauxite ratio control.
equipment.alternatives: Concrete silos with reclaim belt; apron feeder + separate belt scale. Loss-in-weight feeders are not used at these rates.
key_dimensions: Bin live capacity ~500-800 t each (2-3 h at 237 t/h) - engineering estimate
Bin ~8-9 m square/round plan, ~12-15 m high including hopper; hopper walls >= 60-70 deg from horizontal - engineering estimate (confirm with Jenike flow-property tests)
Weigh-belt feeder ~1.2-1.4 m belt width x ~6-8 m centres - engineering estimate
Bin outlet slot ~0.8-1.0 m wide x 3-4 m long - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Typical belt weigh-feeder vendor class (engineering estimate)

equipment.working_principle: The distribution conveyor/tripper delivers crushed bauxite to the top of the bin. It drains under gravity through a steep hopper onto a short belt feeder. The feeder belt runs over a weighing idler mounted on load cells. Belt loading (kg/m) multiplied by belt speed (m/s) gives the wet mass rate, and a moisture value (online microwave/NIR analyser or lab) converts it to dry tph. The DCS adjusts belt speed to hold the dry tph set point, and the mill liquor flow is ratioed to it. Digestion A/C depends directly on the bauxite-to-caustic ratio, so this weigh feeder is one of the most important instruments in the refinery.
details_to_model: Square or circular steel bin on 4-6 steel columns with cross-bracing; roof with the conveyor/tripper gallery entering at the top
Steep transition hopper ending in a long slot outlet; manual rack-and-pinion slide gate with handwheel above the feeder
2-3 external vibrators or air cannons on the hopper walls (aid for blocked chutes)
Radar level transmitter on the roof, high-level switch, inspection hatch with grating
Weigh-belt feeder: head and tail pulleys, skirt boards, weigh idler with load cell, speed wheel, belt scraper at the head pulley, enclosed geared motor with VFD
Feed chute from feeder discharge into the mill feed spout, with a flanged liquor addition pipe entering the chute side
Dust extraction hood and ductwork at bin top and feeder discharge, connected to a bag filter
Belt tracking switches, pull-wire emergency stops along the feeder, guarding on pulleys
Access platform around the feeder with stairs and handrails; storage for calibration chain/test weights
equipment.materials: Bin and hopper carbon steel with abrasion-resistant liners: 400-500 BHN AR plate, or UHMWPE low-friction liners in the hopper. Feeder belt rubber, fabric-ply.
equipment.drive_and_power: Feeder: ~11-22 kW geared motor with VFD (engineering estimate). Bin vibrators ~1-2 kW each.
instrumentation_and_control: Load cell + speed sensor -> tph (WIT/WIC); ratio controller to mill liquor flow FIC
Radar level LT on bin; LSH/LSL
Bauxite moisture analyser (online or lab) for dry-basis correction
Belt rip, misalignment and zero-speed switches
hazards_and_safety: Bin entry is a confined space with engulfment risk (bridged wet bauxite can collapse). Never enter without isolating the feed and holding a permit.
Nip points at feeder pulleys: guarding, and lock-out before belt cleaning
Dust (silica-containing) at transfer points: local exhaust
Working at height on the bin roof
common_problems: Rat-holing/bridging of wet clayey bauxite after rain
Belt build-up causing weigh error; zero drift
Oversize lumps jamming the slot
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check feeder zero/span calibration on schedule - charge control depends on it
Watch for bauxite moisture changes after wet weather and correct the dry-basis factor
Keep bins above minimum level to avoid surging and segregation
sources: Jenike A.W., Storage and Flow of Solids, Bulletin 123, Univ. of Utah (bin design principles)
Adamson, Bloore & Carr (1963) Basic principles of Bayer process design; reprinted in Donaldson & Raahauge (eds), Essential Readings in Light Metals Vol.1, TMS/Wiley 2013 (charge control)

equipment.name: Bauxite ball mills (wet, overflow, closed circuit)
equipment.function: Grind crushed bauxite in hot spent liquor to 100 % < 1 mm, so that desilication and digestion proceed quickly and the slurry is pumpable.
equipment.qty_standby: 1 (installed; lines rotated for relining)
equipment.type_selected: Single-stage wet overflow-discharge ball mill with single-pinion girth-gear drive, in closed circuit with screens.
equipment.why_this_type: Gibbsitic bauxite is relatively soft (Bond Wi typically ~6-14 kWh/t, ore dependent) and only a coarse grind is needed, so a single-stage ball mill in closed circuit is simple and robust. Overflow discharge avoids grate wear in hot caustic. Screens give a sharp 1 mm cut, which cyclones struggle to achieve in dense, viscous caustic slurry.
equipment.alternatives: Rod mill + ball mill two-stage circuit (older refineries); SAG + ball mill, or SAG only, for wet sticky clayey ore; hammer/cage mills for very soft ore. Hydrocyclone classification instead of screens.
key_dimensions: Inside shell diameter ~4.4 m (~4.3 m inside liners), effective grinding length ~6.5 m - engineering estimate from Bond sizing
Overall length including trunnions and trommel ~10-11 m; trommel ~1.8-2.2 m dia x 2.5-3 m long - engineering estimate
Trunnion bore ~1.2-1.5 m - engineering estimate
Centre-line height above floor ~4-4.5 m; foundation pedestals ~3 m high - engineering estimate
Girth gear pitch diameter ~6-7 m - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (Bond equation, Wi ~10 kWh/t, F80 15 mm, P80 300 um; Wills & Finch 2016)
Wills & Finch 2016 (critical speed formula); engineering estimate

CHANGED from 50-75 mm. Bond make-up ball formula B = 25.4 x (F80/K)^0.5 x (SG x Wi / (Cs x sqrt(D_ft)))^(1/3), with K = 350 (wet overflow), F80 15,000-20,000 um, Wi 10-14 kWh/t, SG 2.6, Cs 75 %, D 4.3 m = 14.1 ft. This gives ~75-90 mm (Bond 1958; Wills & Finch 2016 ch.7). 60-75 mm balls are justified only if the crusher product is F80 <= ~6-8 mm. Confirm with Bond Wi test work.

operating_parameters.value: ~90 down to ~40 (worn balls rejected via trommel)

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (mill liquor heated to 88-95 degC with blow-off vapour)

equipment.working_principle: The mill is a horizontal steel cylinder lined with replaceable wear liners. It is about one-third filled with a graded charge of steel balls (make-up ~80 mm, worn down to ~40 mm) and rotates at ~75 % of the speed at which the charge would centrifuge. Lifter bars on the liners carry the balls up the rising side until they cascade and cataract back onto the toe of the charge. Bauxite is broken by impact and ground by abrasion between the balls. The largest balls must be big enough to break the coarsest feed lumps; otherwise these accumulate and raise scats and circulating load. Bauxite and hot liquor enter through the feed trunnion. The discharge trunnion is slightly larger, so slurry overflows out of the discharge end by hydraulic gradient (overflow mill, no grate). A trommel on the discharge trunnion removes scats. Coarse particles are returned from the screens, so the mill only has to finish the material that is still oversize. Throughput is limited by power: power draw rises with ball load and speed, which operators watch via motor kW and bearing pressure.
details_to_model: Shell: cylindrical rolled plate with two bolted/welded cast or fabricated heads. ~300-500 liner bolt heads visible on the shell exterior in a regular grid, with rows matching the lifter rows.
Two rectangular manholes (~600 x 900 mm) on the shell with bolted covers, offset 180 deg

Feed end: feed trunnion with a stationary wear-lined feed chute/spout entering it; liquor addition pipe (DN 150-200) with a flanged spool into the chute; oversize return chute merging into the feed chute

Discharge end: trommel on the discharge trunnion (perforated steel or PU panel screen, ~8-12 mm apertures) inside a closed trommel hood with spray pipe; scats chute to a bunker; slurry falls to the pump box below

Main bearings: two hydrodynamic/hydrostatic trunnion bearings (or shell-supported shoe bearings) on cast pedestals with sole plates. Nearby lube oil skid (tank, HP lift pumps, LP pumps, filters, oil coolers) with piping to the bearings.

Drive: two-half girth gear with a bolted flange joint on a shell flange, enclosed with the pinion in a sheet-metal gear guard. Pinion shaft on two plummer blocks; parallel-shaft gearbox or direct LSD. ~2 MW motor: squirrel cage + VFD, or wound-rotor/synchronous with air clutch. Auxiliary inching drive with overrunning clutch.
Girth gear spray lubrication system (open-gear lube) with nozzles inside the guard

Internals (for cutaway): wave or step shell liners with lifter bars (e.g., 16-20 rows), head liners, graded ball charge (~30 % fill; visibly larger balls near the feed end is acceptable artistic licence), trunnion liners with feed cone
Concrete foundation: two massive pedestals with grouted sole plates; containment floor sloping to a sump, with caustic-resistant coating
Walkways and platforms at bearing and drive levels; interlocked mesh guards around the rotating shell and gear; stairs; kick plates
Mill relining machine (liner handler) parked at the feed end; overhead travelling crane rails above
Instruments: bearing RTDs, oil pressure/flow switches, gear vibration sensors, acoustic mill-load microphone near the shell, motor kW, liquor flowmeter on the feed pipe
equipment.materials: Shell carbon steel plate (e.g., ASTM A516-70 or equivalent). Liners Cr-Mo alloy steel or high-chrome white iron; rubber/PU composite liners only if the hot-caustic rating is confirmed. Balls forged or cast high-chrome steel. Trommel PU or stainless steel panels.
equipment.drive_and_power: ~2.0 MW installed single-pinion girth-gear drive. Motor ~990/1,490 rpm through gearbox or LSD, with VFD or clutch soft-start. Inching drive ~30-55 kW (engineering estimate).
instrumentation_and_control: Mill motor kW and current; mill bearing (load) pressure for charge estimation
Acoustic mill sound sensor ('electronic ear') for load/over-fill
Bearing temperature (RTD) high trips; lube oil flow/pressure permissives
Liquor flow FIC ratioed to bauxite feed WIC
Discharge pump-box level LIC on pump VFD
Online PSD analyser on screen undersize, plus shift sieve tests (% +1 mm, % +300 um)
Interlock sequence: lube system -> mill motor -> feed. Feed stops on mill trip. Inching only with guards closed and under local control.
hazards_and_safety: Rotating equipment: never enter guarding while running; isolate (LOTO) both main and inching drives before entry
Mill entry is a confined space: hot caustic residues, loose liners/balls, frozen charge falling. Ventilate and wash out caustic before entry.
A frozen (cemented) charge can drop when the mill is rotated. Follow the frozen-charge procedure; never use the main drive to break it.

Hot caustic liquor (85-97 degC, pH > 14) splashes at the feed spout, trommel and pump box. Wear chemical goggles + face shield and PVC gloves. Safety showers within 10 s travel (ANSI Z358.1); flush skin for at least 15 min, and eyes much longer (up to 60 min for alkali), then urgent medical review.
Steam/caustic mist at the feed spout and trommel hood because the liquor is close to boiling: hood extraction
Heavy lifting of liners (~0.5-2 t each) and balls with the liner handler/crane
Noise > 90 dB(A) near the mill: hearing protection
common_problems: Overloading (high bearing pressure, falling power, coarse product)
Undersized make-up balls: coarse lumps not broken, rising scats and circulating load
Liner and lifter wear; broken liner bolts leaking slurry
Scale/build-up on the trommel; trommel blinding sends oversize to the pumps
Feed chute blockage with wet sticky ore
Coarse grind leading to sanding in pre-desilication tanks and slow digestion
operating_tips_and_key_points: Charge control: keep the liquor-to-bauxite ratio steady. A step in bauxite tph changes digester A/C ~8-12 hours later, after passing through the storage and desilication tanks.
Watch % +1 mm in the product; worn or holed screen panels let coarse particles through
Add balls of the specified make-up size on a kWh or tonnage schedule to maintain power draw
Check trunnion seals and liner bolts for caustic leaks every shift
sources: Wills B.A. & Finch J.A. (2016) Wills' Mineral Processing Technology, 8th ed. (Bond equation, critical speed Nc = 42.3/sqrt(D), Bond make-up ball size)
Bond F.C. (1958) Grinding ball size selection, Mining Engineering 10:592-595
Rowland C.A. & Kjos D.M., Rod and ball mills, in SME Mineral Processing Plant Design (ball mill sizing)
Adamson, Bloore & Carr (1963), reprinted in Essential Readings in Light Metals Vol.1 (TMS/Wiley 2013) - bauxite grinding in spent liquor
Engineering estimate (mill size, power) - to be confirmed by Bond Wi test work on project bauxite

equipment.name: Mill discharge pumps
equipment.function: Lift mill discharge slurry from each pump box to the screen flow divider.
equipment.qty_standby: 5. Arrangement: 4 mill lines x (1 duty + 1 installed standby) = 8 pumps, 3 running.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction heavy-duty centrifugal slurry pump with hard-metal (27 % Cr white iron) replaceable liners and impeller, expeller (dynamic) seal or cartridge mechanical seal, VFD drive.
equipment.why_this_type: Abrasive slurry at modest head (~25-35 m) and high flow is the ideal duty for hard-metal centrifugal slurry pumps. Rubber liners are avoided because of the 85-97 degC caustic. Gland water flushing is minimised because water dilutes the liquor and adds evaporation load.
equipment.alternatives: Vertical cantilever sump pumps (smaller duties); rubber-lined pumps only where temperature and chemistry allow.
key_dimensions: Discharge nozzle ~DN 250-300, suction ~DN 300-350 (e.g., '12/10' frame) - engineering estimate
Impeller ~900-1,100 mm dia - engineering estimate
Pump + motor base ~4-5 m long x 1.5-2 m wide - engineering estimate
equipment.working_principle: The impeller spins inside a thick hard-metal volute liner. Slurry enters the eye axially and the vanes accelerate it outward; the volute converts its velocity to pressure. Expeller vanes on the back of the impeller, plus a separate expeller, keep slurry away from the shaft seal while running. The VFD varies speed to hold pump-box level. Large clearances, thick wear sections and an adjustable impeller-to-throatbush gap make the pump tolerant of abrasive bauxite. Because the slurry is only ~10 K below its boiling point, the pump box level provides most of the NPSH margin.
details_to_model: Split outer casing (two cast iron halves bolted at a vertical joint) enclosing the white-iron volute liner, throatbush and frame-plate liner insert
Closed impeller with 4-5 vanes and pump-out vanes on the shrouds
Cartridge bearing assembly on the base with impeller adjustment bolts
Expeller/gland seal housing, or mechanical seal with quench line
Suction spool from the pump box with knife-gate isolation valve and flushing/drain connection. Discharge with diaphragm-seal pressure gauge, knife gate or plug valve, and dismantling joint.
Drive: overhead-mounted motor with V-belt drive and belt guard, or direct coupled with gearbox
Pump box above: steel hopper with wear liner, overflow to sump, level transmitter, liquor addition pipe, vent hood
Concrete plinth, drip tray and bunded floor
equipment.materials: High-chrome white iron (~27 % Cr) liners and impeller; cast or ductile iron outer casing; alloy steel shaft; elastomer seals rated for hot caustic (e.g., EPDM - confirm with vendor).
equipment.drive_and_power: 160-250 kW induction motor with VFD (engineering estimate).
instrumentation_and_control: Pump-box level LIC -> VFD speed
Discharge pressure PI/PT
Motor current; bearing temperature/vibration (optional)
Low-flow/dry-run protection via level permissive
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry (85-97 degC): seal leaks spray. Spray shields on flanges.
Opening drains/flush lines can release hot caustic; drain to bund first
Rotating belt drive: guarding, LOTO
common_problems: Liner wear and impeller nose wear (falling head)
Air entrainment/surging, or cavitation of near-boiling slurry, when pump-box level is low
Blockage by scats if the trommel is damaged
operating_tips_and_key_points: Adjust impeller clearance regularly to restore performance
Flush the line with liquor before stopping to prevent sanding
sources: Weir Minerals, Warman Slurry Pumping Handbook

equipment.name: Mill circuit high-frequency multi-deck screens
equipment.function: Classify mill discharge at ~1.0 mm. Undersize is product to slurry storage; oversize returns to the mill.
equipment.qty_standby: 4 (installed with the standby mill line); any screen can be isolated at its feed valve
equipment.type_selected: High-frequency multi-deck linear-motion wet screen (Derrick Stack Sizer type): ~5 decks stacked and fed in parallel, polyurethane panels with ~1.0 mm apertures.
equipment.why_this_type: Gives a sharp size cut at ~1 mm in dense, viscous caustic slurry that does not depend on particle density. Heavy iron-rich particles are not over-recycled, as they would be in hydrocyclones. Stacked decks give high capacity per floor area.
equipment.alternatives: Hydrocyclone clusters (cheaper, finer cut, but density-driven); DSM sieve bends; trommel-only classification.
key_dimensions: Each deck ~1.2 m wide x ~2.4 m long; 5 decks stacked ~0.4-0.5 m apart; overall unit ~2.5 m W x 4.5 m L x 4.5 m H - engineering estimate
Screen floor elevation ~+12 to +15 m above grade - engineering estimate
equipment.working_principle: A flow divider splits the mill discharge evenly between the screens and between the decks of each screen. Two counter-rotating unbalanced vibrator motors (~3,000 rpm class, low amplitude) give a high-frequency linear motion. This conveys oversize along the deck toward the discharge end while liquor and fine particles pass through the polyurethane apertures. Undersize from all decks collects in a common pan and launder. Oversize from each deck joins a common chute back to the mill feed. Spray bars of hot spent liquor help wash fines through; liquor is used rather than water to avoid dilution.
details_to_model: Overhead feed distributor (multi-outlet flow divider) with flexible hoses to each deck's feed box
Stack of 5 inclined decks with modular PU panels (~300 x 600 mm on cross-members)
Pair of vibrator motors on top of the frame; rubber/coil spring isolators at the four corners
Oversize chutes at the discharge end merging into a single chute; undersize collection pan sloping to the launder
Hoods/covers with vent ducts to a scrubber (caustic mist and steam)
Spray bars with valves; liquor header
Elevated steel screen floor with grating, handrails and stairs; monorail hoist above for panel and motor changes
equipment.materials: Painted carbon steel frame; PU screen panels; stainless or lined chutes/launders.
equipment.drive_and_power: 2 vibrator motors per screen, ~2 kW each (engineering estimate).
instrumentation_and_control: Feed distributor level/overflow indicator
Vibration monitoring (motor run status)
Undersize PSD sampling (auto-sampler) and screen-efficiency checks per shift
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic mist and splashes around screens: face shield, enclosure
Moving vibrating frame: keep clear, LOTO for panel changes
Working at height on the screen floor
common_problems: Panel blinding/pegging with near-size particles
Torn panels causing coarse product
Uneven feed distribution overloading a deck
operating_tips_and_key_points: Inspect panels every shift; a single holed panel sends oversize to digestion
Balance flow to all decks
sources: Derrick Corporation, Stack Sizer product literature (alumina/bauxite applications)

equipment.name: Ground slurry storage tanks
equipment.function: Provide ~4-5 h surge of ground bauxite slurry between grinding and pre-desilication/digestion, keeping solids suspended and homogenised.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each tank can be bypassed; plant then runs with reduced surge)
equipment.type_selected: Vertical flat-bottomed atmospheric steel tank (API 650 construction) with a top-entry, two-stage axial-flow (hydrofoil/pitched-blade) agitator and wall baffles.
equipment.why_this_type: Large-volume slurry surge at atmospheric pressure. Agitated flat-bottomed tanks are the standard Bayer slurry storage design.
equipment.alternatives: Cone-bottomed tanks (smaller sizes); combining storage with the first pre-desilication tanks.
key_dimensions: ~14 m ID x ~14-15 m shell height; ~2,100-2,300 m3 gross, ~1,900 m3 working each - engineering estimate
Agitator: 2 impellers, D/T ~0.30-0.35 (~4.3-4.8 m dia), lower impeller ~1/4 T off bottom - engineering estimate
4 wall baffles, width ~T/12 (~1.15 m), with a gap from the wall - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (~0.08-0.12 kW/m3 for this slurry)

equipment.working_principle: Undersize slurry enters through a top inlet. The top-mounted agitator drives large, slow axial-flow impellers that pump slurry down the centre and up the walls. Baffles stop the contents swirling as a whole and convert rotation into vertical mixing, so bauxite particles up to 1 mm, including heavy iron minerals, stay suspended. Transfer pumps draw slurry from a bottom side outlet. Because the tanks are well mixed, short-term changes in grind or charge ratio are smoothed out before digestion. Some desilication already starts here.
details_to_model: Cylindrical shell with ~8-10 visible horizontal weld courses; cone or flat roof with a roof girder (steel box-beam agitator bridge spanning the roof)
Agitator drive on the bridge: vertical motor, right-angle gearbox, shaft ~250-300 mm through a roof seal, two impellers; optional steady bearing
Nozzles: inlet DN 400-600 at the roof from the gravity launder; outlet DN 400-450 near the bottom with knife-gate valve; drain DN 200; overflow DN 500 to bund
4 internal baffles; bottom 'scour' area; two DN 900 manways in the bottom shell course; roof manway
Radar level on the roof; vent with steam/caustic mist duct to scrubber
Insulation (mineral wool ~50-75 mm) with aluminium cladding; concrete ring-beam foundation
Spiral stair around the shell to the roof; roof handrail; bunded concrete area with sump
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (API 650), corrosion allowance ~3 mm. PWHT/stress relief of nozzle and attachment welds per the caustic SCC chart in NACE SP0403 (plant-wide materials philosophy to be confirmed by owner). Agitator wetted parts carbon steel with hard-faced blade tips.
equipment.drive_and_power: 150-250 kW motor + helical-bevel gearbox per tank (engineering estimate). Essential (emergency diesel) supply recommended so agitators can restart before solids settle.
instrumentation_and_control: Radar LT/LIC (transfer pump speed); LAH/LAL

areas.purpose: Hold the ground bauxite slurry near its atmospheric boiling point (~98-102 degC) for ~8-10 h so that most of the reactive silica (kaolinite) dissolves and re-precipitates as sodalite-type desilication product (DSP) before digestion. This lowers dissolved silica in the digestion stream, which cuts DSP scale in the liquor heaters, slurry steam injectors and digesters and controls SiO2 in pregnant liquor (and therefore in product alumina). A05 also delivers the desilicated slurry from its 2 strings to the 3 digestion units through a common digestion feed tank.
areas.process_description:
1) Ground slurry (~85-93 degC) from storage (A04) is pumped in two parallel strings of ~415 m3/h each.
2) In each string a direct-contact steam-injection heater uses LP steam (~3.5-5 barg) to raise the slurry to 98-102 degC. The steam condenses directly into the slurry, adding ~15-30 t/h of water in total, which must later be removed in evaporation. The slurry boils at ~105-107 degC because of boiling-point elevation, so the tanks run atmospheric.
3) Slurry flows by gravity overflow through three agitated, insulated tanks in series per string (6 tanks, ~1,500 m3 working each). Both strings then overflow into a common agitated digestion feed tank (05-TK-007, ~1,000 m3 working). Nominal residence is ~11-12 h with all tanks on line and ~9-10 h with one desilication tank out for descaling (engineering estimate; typical practice 6-12 h).
4) Chemistry. Kaolinite dissolves: Al2Si2O5(OH)4 + 6 NaOH -> 2 NaAl(OH)4 + 2 Na2SiO3 + H2O. The dissolved silica reacts with aluminate to precipitate sodalite: 6 Na2SiO3 + 6 NaAl(OH)4 + Na2X -> Na6[Al6Si6O24].Na2X + 12 NaOH + 6 H2O, where X = CO3(2-), SO4(2-), 2Cl-, 2OH- etc. It is often written 3(Na2O.Al2O3.2SiO2.nH2O).Na2X. The DSP stays with the residue. Stoichiometrically, each tonne of reactive SiO2 locks up ~0.85 t Al2O3 and ~0.69 t Na2O (as Na8 sodalite), which is why reactive silica is the main driver of caustic consumption. At design 2 % reactive SiO2 (~12.8 t/h SiO2) this is ~34 t/h DSP, with ~11 t/h Al2O3 and ~9 t/h Na2O lost (engineering estimate). Target: ~70-90 % of reactive silica converted to DSP before digestion; the rest completes in digestion. Quartz is essentially inert at <= 150 degC.
5) Desilication rate improves with temperature, time, DSP seed (recycled solids) and fine grind. Low caustic slows it.
6) Desilicated slurry (~44-47 % solids, ~860 m3/h, 98-102 degC) leaves 05-TK-007 to the digestion slurry charge pump trains of the three digestion units (A06), one train per unit. Each train takes ~287 m3/h from a common suction header.
High-temperature plants: pre-desilication is similar, but much of the desilication also occurs in the high-temperature digesters, and some plants use pressure pre-desilication at higher temperature.

areas.purpose: Dissolve the gibbsite in the bauxite into hot caustic liquor at ~145 degC (low-temperature digestion), raising liquor A/C from ~0.37 (spent) to ~0.70-0.74. Thermal efficiency comes from regenerative heating of the spent liquor stream with flash vapour, final indirect heating of the liquor with live steam, and direct live-steam injection into the slurry stream. This 'double-stream' arrangement with liquor-only indirect heating is the base case for the reference plant (CHANGED from the draft, which also had flash-vapour slurry heaters and PD pumps; those are now a documented option only).
areas.process_description:
Design basis: double-stream regenerative low-temperature digestion. There are 3 parallel digestion units, each ~1/3 of plant capacity (~80 t/h Al2O3). The unit count is an engineering estimate; real low-temperature refineries of this size use 2-5 units. Per unit:
1) Slurry stream. ~287 m3/h of desilicated slurry (~44-47 % solids, ~100 degC) is taken from the digestion feed tank 05-TK-007. Two hard-metal centrifugal slurry pumps in series (one duty train + one standby train) raise it to ~12-14 barg. Two in-line direct live-steam injection heaters in series (06-SI) then heat it from ~100 degC to ~130-140 degC (design ~138). No slurry heat-transfer surfaces are used, which avoids the rapid DSP/kaolinite fouling that slurry tube heaters suffer.
2) Liquor stream. Strong spent liquor from evaporation (~700-730 m3/h per unit, C ~270-290 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C ~0.37, ~90-100 degC) is pumped by high-head centrifugal liquor pumps (~15-20 barg) through 6 flash-vapour LIQUOR HEATERS (liquor in tubes, flash vapour on shell, stage 6 -> 1) to ~128-131 degC. Two LIVE-STEAM LIQUOR HEATERS (MP steam 10-12 barg, ~184-192 degC) then take it to ~158-166 degC (design 162). The liquor is therefore 'superheated' relative to the digestion temperature.
3) Both streams enter digester 1 through a mixing inlet. The heat in the superheated liquor plus the slurry injection steam brings the mixture to 143-150 degC (design 145) after the gibbsite dissolution endotherm. The slurry injection steam rate is the fine temperature trim (TIC on digester 1/2 outlet).
4) The slurry flows under pressure through 4 agitated digesters in series. Residence is ~55-60 min with all 4 on line and ~40-45 min with one bypassed. Main reaction: Al(OH)3(s) + NaOH(aq) -> NaAl(OH)4(aq). Gibbsite dissolution is endothermic (~0.45-0.55 GJ/t Al2O3 dissolved - engineering estimate, verify) and fast at 145 degC, typically complete within ~10-30 min. DSP precipitation completes. Quartz, hematite, goethite and anatase stay largely unreacted; quartz attack is negligible at <= 150 degC, a key advantage of low-temperature digestion. BOEHMITE in gibbsitic ore (typically ~0.5-5 % of the bauxite, e.g. Darling Range and some India East Coast ores) is largely NOT extracted at 145 degC. It reports to residue and is counted in total Al2O3 but not in available Al2O3. Undissolved boehmite (and hematite/goethite surfaces) can seed 'boehmite reversion' of dissolved alumina once the liquor becomes supersaturated on cooling. The time from blow-off to settler overflow (A07-A08) is therefore kept short, and digester exit A/C is held below the reversion-risk limit. Part of the organic carbon (humates) degrades to oxalate, carbonate and low-MW organics. Digester exit liquor A/C is ~0.70-0.74.
5) Digested slurry (~980-1,040 m3/h per unit, ~145 degC) is let down into the flash train (A07). Flash vapour from stages 1-6 returns to the liquor heaters. The surplus atmospheric blow-off vapour goes to the A04 mill liquor heater and the A07 surface vent condensers or evaporation.
Heat balance per unit (engineering estimate). Demand ~68-72 MW:
- liquor 95 -> 145 degC: ~43 MW
- slurry 100 -> 145 degC: ~14 MW
- dissolution endotherm: ~10-12 MW
- losses: ~1.5 MW
Flash vapour recovered in the liquor heaters is ~30 MW. The liquor heat sink is limited to <~131 degC by the flash vapour temperatures, and the liquor's heat-capacity flow (~0.87 MW/K) is smaller than that of the digested slurry (~1.29 MW/K). Live steam therefore supplies ~38-42 MW: liquor heaters ~27-30 MW (~48-55 t/h) and slurry injection ~9-12 MW (~15-22 t/h), ~65-75 t/h per unit in total. This is ~0.8-0.95 t steam/t Al2O3, vs ~0.55-0.7 t/t with the slurry-heater option.
Operating pressure: digester 1 is held at ~6-7 barg. That is above the vapour pressure of the incoming 162 degC liquor (~4.6 barg with BPE ~6 K) and well above the mixture vapour pressure at 145 degC (~2.5-3 barg). The last digester runs at ~5-6.5 barg under PIC on the let-down valve. Design: 10 barg at 200 degC (CHANGED from 9 barg/175 degC - see 06-DG).
Sweetening: not used in this base design (the bauxite is essentially all gibbsite). In plants that digest mixed gibbsite/boehmite ore at high temperature, extra gibbsitic slurry ('sweetening') is injected into the hot digested slurry in the first flash stages to raise A/C. Mention for trainees only.
High-temperature (boehmitic/diasporic) plants differ:
- 230-280 degC at ~30-60 barg, with PD (GEHO-type) pumps to 60-100+ bar
- slurry heaters (shell & tube or tube-in-tube) with 8-12+ flash stages
- tube digesters or autoclaves with indirect heating (molten salt in some plants)
- lime addition to control titanate scale
- quartz attack and higher caustic loss; boehmite/titanate scales

areas.layout_notes:
Three digestion units in parallel bays, each ~25-30 m wide x ~60-70 m long (engineering estimate), with a common 3-tier pipe rack (~+6/+9/+12 m) along the bays. In each bay:
- The two slurry charge pump trains are at grade at the feed end, nearest 05-TK-007, with monorails. The liquor pumps (fed from 06-TK-101) are beside them.
- The heater bank structure is ~3 levels, ~12-15 m tall: 9 identical liquor heaters per unit (6 flash, 2 live-steam, 1 spare) stacked 2-3 high, with platforms at the channel-cover levels.
- The slurry steam injectors sit on the rising slurry line beside digester 1.
- The digesters stand in a straight row on a structure/skirts, top platforms at ~+20-22 m linked by walkways, with a stair tower.
- The flash train (A07) is stepped down beside the digesters, with each flash tank opposite its paired liquor heater so the vapour lines are short and slope back with no pockets.
The live-steam header, PRDS and SIS steam shut-off valves are on the rack. Allow ~3 m at each heater end for channel-cover removal and lance frames, and a ~6 m crane access roadway along each bay. The relief header slopes to the shared dump tank and quench stack at the end of the area; the stack is placed downwind and away from walkways. Safety showers at every level/stair landing.

A18 Evaporation/spent liquor: strong spent liquor to 06-TK-101
A07 Flash cooling: digested slurry out; flash vapour (stages 1-6) in to the liquor heaters; heater condensate out to the A07 condensate system
A20 Power house/steam: MP steam 10-12 barg (~190-230 t/h, CHANGED); clean condensate return (~145-165 t/h); boiler feed water for desuperheating

areas.purpose: Cool the digested slurry from ~145 degC to its atmospheric boiling point (~106-107 degC) in pressure steps. Each step produces flash vapour at a successively lower pressure, which heats the incoming spent liquor (regenerative heat recovery). Collect the condensate for reuse, and route the surplus atmospheric blow-off vapour to useful sinks or surface vent condensers. Deliver the blow-off slurry to the A08 sand cyclones with a single pumping step.
areas.process_description:
1) Digested slurry from the last digester is let down through a severe-service control valve (which holds digester pressure) into flash tank 1.
2) In each of 6 pressurised flash tanks per unit the pressure is below the vapour pressure of the incoming slurry. Part of the water boils instantly (flashes) until the slurry cools to the boiling temperature at that pressure. In the liquor-only base case the slurry cools ~3.9-4 K per pressurised stage, and ~0.55-0.6 % of its mass evaporates per stage (fraction = cp x dT / hfg = 3.15 x 4 / 2,180).
3) Vapour leaves each tank top through a disengagement space/baffle to the paired liquor heater in A06. Slurry from the tank bottom passes through a level-control (let-down) valve to the next, lower-pressure tank.
4) Indicative stage table (engineering estimate; slurry exit T / vapour saturation T / pressure):
- FT1: 141 / 135 degC, ~3.13 bar a (~2.1 barg)
- FT2: 137 / 131 degC, ~2.78 bar a
- FT3: 133.5 / 127.5 degC, ~2.51 bar a
- FT4: 129.5 / 123.5 degC, ~2.22 bar a
- FT5: 125.5 / 119.5 degC, ~1.95 bar a
- FT6: 121.5 / 115.5 degC, ~1.72 bar a (~0.7 barg)
- Atmospheric blow-off tank: ~106-107 degC
The vapour is saturated at a lower temperature than the slurry because the caustic liquor has a boiling-point elevation of ~5-7 K. Pressures are from IAPWS-IF97. CHANGED from the draft table (139/133 ... 109/103 degC), which assumed paired slurry + liquor heaters.
5) Blow-off (atmospheric) tank. With liquor-only heating the liquor (~0.87 MW/K) cannot absorb all the heat released by the slurry (~1.29 MW/K) at temperatures below ~131 degC. The final flash from ~121.5 to ~106 degC is therefore large: ~30-33 t/h vapour per unit (~1.8-2 % of slurry mass), ~90-100 t/h in total. Over all stages to atmospheric, ~5.5-6 % of the slurry mass evaporates. Blow-off vapour goes to:
(a) the A04 mill liquor heater (~13-20 t/h total);
(b) as an option to be confirmed by A18, an intermediate evaporator effect;
(c) the rest to surface (shell & tube) vent condensers on cooling water, which recover the condensate.
The slurry is pumped by 07-PP-001..006 directly to the A08 sand cyclones. Cyclone overflow goes to the A08 dilution/settler feed tank, where it is diluted with first-washer overflow. Residence from blow-off to settler overflow is kept short to limit boehmite/gibbsite reversion.
6) Condensate. Liquor heater condensate from each stage drains via condensate pots and cascades to the next lower-pressure pot, re-flashing. It is finally collected as 'process condensate' (~50 t/h per unit), together with the vent-condenser and mill-liquor-heater condensate (~25-33 t/h per unit). The total is ~230-250 t/h (~0.95-1.0 t/t Al2O3). It is monitored by conductivity for caustic contamination and sent to the plant process condensate tank (18-TK-012, owned by A18) for residue/hydrate washing or polishing. Live-steam condensate is kept separate ('clean condensate') and returned to the boilers after conductivity checks.
7) Non-condensable gases from the heater shells are bled stage to stage. The last stage and the blow-off tank vent to the vent condensers (odour/VOC control).
8) Scale control. Gibbsite (from alumina supersaturation as the slurry cools) and DSP scale form on flash tank walls, inlet boxes and interstage lines/valves. These are inspected and descaled at unit shutdowns (~6-12 months, engineering estimate) by UHP water jetting or mechanical means, and erosion-resistant inserts are replaced.
High-temperature plants: typically 8-12+ flash stages from ~250 degC, much higher first-stage pressures (~20-30 bar), and titanate/boehmite scales.

equipment.working_principle: Hot slurry enters through the let-down valve at a pressure above the tank's saturation pressure. On entering the lower-pressure tank some of its water boils instantly, absorbing latent heat and cooling the slurry to the saturation temperature at the tank pressure plus the boiling-point elevation. The violent two-phase jet strikes a replaceable impact box rather than the shell. Vapour rises through the disengagement height, where droplets fall back, and leaves through the top nozzle to the paired liquor heater. Condensation in that heater is what holds the tank pressure down. Slurry collects in the cone and passes to the next tank through a level-control valve. More stages bring the liquor closer to the slurry temperature but need more equipment.

areas.layout_notes: Each unit's flash train runs in a straight line or L beside its digesters. Tanks are stepped down ~2-3 m per stage on a common steel structure (tops from ~+20 m down to ~+8 m), so interstage slurry flows by pressure difference and gravity. Each flash tank stands opposite its paired liquor heater in the A06 heater bank, so vapour lines (DN 300-450) are short and slope back with no pockets. FT1 is the heaviest vessel (10 barg rating). The blow-off tank is elevated (bottom ~+8-10 m) above its transfer pumps. A large blow-off vapour header (DN 900-1,200) runs on the rack to the mill liquor heater (A04) and the surface vent condenser at the end of the train. Condensate pots sit under each heater; the condensate collection tanks and pumps are at the end of the heater bank. Platforms at each tank top and inlet level are linked by walkways and a stair tower. A maintenance roadway along the train gives crane access for cone and wear-box replacement. Distance to the A08 sand cyclones/dilution is ~100-200 m (engineering estimate).

decisions.finding: A06 flowsheet: make liquor-only regenerative heating the base case, with slurry pumped centrifugally and heated by live-steam injection; slurry heaters/PD pumps as an option; redo the duty split (process reviewer)
decisions.reason: Agreed that this is more representative of low-temperature gibbsitic practice and avoids slurry-heater DSP fouling. Applied: slurry heaters (06-HX-101..121) and PD pumps (06-PD) moved to a documented OPTION entry; new 06-PP-001..012 centrifugal charge pumps (2 in series) and 06-SI-001..006 slurry injectors added. Heat balance redone. The reviewer's premise that the liquor heaters 'must absorb all ~45-48 MW' is thermodynamically impossible: the liquor heat-capacity flow (~0.87 MW/K) is below that of the digested slurry (~1.29 MW/K), and flash vapour is <~135 degC. The liquor heaters therefore recover ~30 MW per unit. Live steam rises to ~0.8-0.95 t/t, and ~90-100 t/h of surplus blow-off vapour is routed to the mill liquor heater, A18 (option) or surface condensers. Flash stage table, heater count (48 -> 27) and condensate pots (48 -> 27) were updated.
